nodes.summary: For every target power `β < 1` there is a cohort size beyond which the power is at least `β` (Lawrence et al. 2014 take `β = 0.9`).
nodes.title: `N_β` exists

nodes.summary: A driver mutated above background raises the per-patient probability: `p₀ < p₀ + r (1 - m)` for `r > 0` and `m < 1`.
nodes.title: Driver genes raise the per-patient mutation probability

nodes.summary: The background probability is a probability below one: `0 ≤ p₀ < 1` for `0 ≤ μ f_g < 1` and `L ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Background mutation probability lies in (0, 1)

nodes.summary: Background probability `p₀ = 1 - (1 - μ f_g)^(3L/4)` that a patient carries at least one non-silent background mutation in a gene of `L` coding bases (Lawrence et al. 2014).
nodes.title: Background mutation probability per patient

nodes.summary: Signal probability `p₁ = p₀ + r (1 - m)` for a gene mutated in a fraction `r` of patients above background, with miss rate `m` (Lawrence et al. 2014).
nodes.title: Signal mutation probability per patient

nodes.summary: Power of the one-sided binomial test of Lawrence et al. (2014): the probability, when each of `N` patients is mutated with probability `p₁`, of observing a count `x` whose background p-value `ℙ_{p₀}(X ≥ x)` is at most `γ`.
nodes.title: Saturation power of the binomial gene discovery test

nodes.summary: For `0 ≤ p₀ < p₁ ≤ 1` and any level `γ > 0`, the power of the binomial test tends to `1` as the number of patients grows.
nodes.title: Power tends to one

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.
